hero_copy.headline: 77% of Jaipur's piped water comes from a dam about {km} km away
hero_copy.body: The Public Health Engineering Department (PHED), the state's water department, produced 766.73 MLD a day for {city} at the end of 2025. 590 MLD came from Bisalpur dam on the Banas and 176 MLD from 3,633 PHED tube wells. A year earlier Bisalpur gave 492 MLD: the whole rise of about 98 MLD came from the dam. Bisalpur is shared: a Water Resources Department study (2020) describes 11.1 TMC a year for Jaipur and the villages on its pipeline, 5.1 TMC for Ajmer, and the rest for irrigation. PHED's zone schedule (April 2024) gives most colonies about an hour of water a day.
hero_copy.wtp_sub: 590 MLD from Bisalpur and 176 MLD from 3,633 tube wells, 31 December 2025
hero_copy.uphill_sub: Distance JICA gives for the transfer system (2016)
hero_copy.footer: Figures from PHED Rajasthan's Annual Progress Reports 2025-26 (status 31 December 2025, p.85) and 2024-25 (p.84), and PHED's zone schedule of 15 April 2024. PHED publishes no city-wide non-revenue water and no order fixing Jaipur's share of Bisalpur; both are named gaps on the About page.

PHED's city pumping stations and reservoirs (City Circles North and South)
3,633 PHED tube wells pumping into the same network
